tasks.short: Read utility meters and record readings

steps.what: Locate and match the actual electric, gas, water or steam meter to the route account and physical meter identity
inputs: actual assigned route and existing account/meter identifiers
actual accessible meter and physical identifier

steps.what: Read electric, gas, water or steam consumption meters, checking the actual display, units and reading condition
inputs: reader-confirmed actual meter/account match
actual meter display and condition
outputs: reader's actual observed consumption reading, units and uncertainty

steps.what: Enter data in the hand-held meter route computer (OPS_SYSTEM) and check the actual reading, units, meter identity and intended route record
inputs: reader's actual observed consumption reading, units and uncertainty
reader-confirmed actual meter/account match and existing route context
outputs: exact checked actual meter-reading entry and route destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked actual consumption reading in the intended hand-held route record
inputs: exact checked actual meter-reading entry and route destination

tasks.design: For the existing hand-held route-computer route, configure fixed route/account context in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the utility meter-reading application. The reader physically matches and reads the actual meter, enters its real reading and checks the completed entry before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated route/account identifiers add entry work around physical readings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native hand-held route context can reuse existing fixed identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Correct physical meter identity, display interpretation and access conditions require field work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unreadable or mismatched meters without inventing a reading.

ambition.what: No new smart-meter feed or automated billing decision.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; route-system owner validates device access and meter/account context

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native hand-held route context can reduce repeated identifiers while actual physical meter matching and reading remain reader work.

assumptions: Unmeasured existing hand-held entry episode, a stated alternative to paper route books. Gross 34 x .10 = 3.4; upkeep 1; net 2.4 hours per 100.

Route office already supplies actual assigned account/meter identifiers; reader physically matches in s1 and produces/captures the reading in s2-s3. No free telemetry, OCR or newly structured reading.
Only fixed identifier/navigation entry changes; actual reading and checking stay. If current route context already supplies identifiers, benefit is zero.
Same-system save 1 stays fully retained with no saving. Final completed-entry check s3 gates exact content/meter/route; edits require recheck. Office upload is a separate task, not hidden here.
unknowns: Actual repeated identifiers in current route application
research_questions: Which fields are retyped after route download, and how is physical meter identity confirmed?

already_counted.description: Physical meter matching/reading and actual entry/check

incremental.description: Maintain and spot-check route/account context mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed actual reading, units and meter/route destination checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 fixed-entry scenario below 2.4% modeled net; no physical reading or save-click saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify the actual completed hand-held meter round, device, office destination and outstanding route exceptions
inputs: actual completed hand-held route dataset
actual device/round identifiers and intended office collection system
outputs: reader-identified actual round dataset and intended office destination

steps.what: Prepare and inspect the complete actual route upload package, account/meter keys, counts and transfer configuration in meter route transfer software (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: reader-identified actual round dataset and intended office destination
actual office import schema and permitted transfer profile
outputs: complete prepared actual round upload package and transfer configuration

steps.what: Check the exact final meter-round upload payload, actual counts/identities, exceptions and intended office system destination
inputs: complete prepared actual round upload package and transfer configuration
actual source round dataset and office destination
outputs: exact checked final upload payload/configuration and office destination

steps.what: Upload into office computers all information collected on hand-held computers during the actual meter round by committing the exact checked upload
inputs: exact checked final upload payload/configuration and office destination
outputs: actual office upload result, accepted/rejected rows and native receipt

steps.what: Verify the actual office receipt and accepted/rejected counts against the hand-held round, investigating mismatches and retaining source data until resolved
inputs: actual office upload result, accepted/rejected rows and native receipt
actual completed source round and expected counts
outputs: reader-verified upload completeness or unresolved discrepancy requiring corrected re-upload

tasks.design: For the hand-held upload alternative, configure a native known-schema transfer profile in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the meter route transfer system. The reader prepares and checks the actual final upload, commits it to the office destination and verifies the resulting receipt and row counts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated transfer-profile and field setup adds round upload administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native route transfer profiles can reuse a stable office import schema.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong round identity, rejected rows and incomplete transfer require actual reconciliation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise incomplete upload and preserve the source until resolved.

ambition.what: No automatic billing or silent deletion of hand-held data.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; route/office system owners validate transfer permissions and schema

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native meter-route transfer profiles can reduce repeated mapping/setup while upload completeness requires source-to-receipt verification.

assumptions: Unmeasured hand-held upload episode, the statement's digital alternative; physical return of books/devices is not made free. Gross 39 x .10 = 3.9; upkeep 1; net 2.9 hours per 100.
Reader already captured actual readings during the round; selects/prepares/checks the actual dataset in s1-s3. No free new structured readings or uncounted office re-key.
Only repeated transfer setup changes. Upload execution/runtime already exists today and earns no saving; commit click 1 stays fully retained with no saving.

s3 checks exact final payload/configuration/destination before s4; edits require recheck. Actual receipt verification occurs after upload in s5. A corrected retry returns through preparation and final gate rather than automatic resend.
Native receipt is the system record; no separate undocumented save or new completion notification is promised. No source deletion is proposed.
unknowns: Actual native transfer setup already in place
research_questions: Which transfer configuration is genuinely repeated, and how are actual rejected rows reconciled?

already_counted.description: Round identification, remaining transfer preparation, final payload check and actual receipt reconciliation

incremental.description: Maintain and test route/office schema transfer profile

approvals.approved_version: Exact final actual round payload, transfer configuration and office destination checked in s3; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 native transfer-setup scenario below 2.9% modeled net; upload click/runtime retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify abnormal readings and record reasons

steps.what: Read actual abnormal-consumption flag, current/prior readings, meter identity and relevant route history in meter reading records (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual existing abnormal-consumption flag or actual office verification request
actual meter/account identity and available prior/current readings

steps.what: Verify readings where consumption appears abnormal by matching and re-reading the actual meter and checking display, units and observable conditions
inputs: reader-reviewed actual abnormal-reading context
actual meter identity, display and observable conditions
outputs: reader's verified actual reading and observed conditions or unresolved uncertainty

steps.what: Assess possible reasons for actual consumption fluctuations, distinguishing observed facts, customer information and unconfirmed hypotheses
inputs: reader's verified actual reading and observed conditions or unresolved uncertainty
actual available history and any real customer explanation
outputs: reader's supported possible reasons and explicit unknowns

steps.what: Record possible reasons for fluctuations and actual verification facts, then check the complete reading/exception entry and intended meter/account record
inputs: reader's supported possible reasons and explicit unknowns
reader's verified actual reading and observed conditions or unresolved uncertainty
actual meter/account identifiers
outputs: exact checked verification/reason entry and meter/account destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked actual abnormal-reading verification and possible-reason entry in its intended meter/account record
inputs: exact checked verification/reason entry and meter/account destination
outputs: saved actual abnormal-reading verification and reason record

tasks.design: Configure current/prior reading views and fixed meter/account context in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the meter reading record system. The reader rechecks the physical meter, assesses only supported possible reasons and checks the completed actual exception entry before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated history lookup and identifiers add exception-record work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native meter-context views and entry forms can reduce navigation/fixed fields.
tasks.still_hard: A fluctuation may have multiple causes and a plausible explanation is not a verified cause.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish actual re-reading and observed facts from unconfirmed reasons.

ambition.what: No automatic diagnosis, account correction or billing change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; meter-record owner validates access and exception fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native meter history/context views can reduce exception-record handling while actual abnormal reading verification remains physical and judgmental work.

assumptions: Unmeasured flagged-reading verification episode. Gross 20 x .10 + 19 x .10 = 3.9; upkeep 1; net 2.9 hours per 100.

Existing office rules/staff provide the actual flag/request and history; reader retrieves them in s1, produces real re-reading/observations in s2 and captures actual reasons/uncertainty in s3-s4. No new sensor data, free reason codes or inferred cause.
Only navigation/fixed identifiers change. All physical verification, cause assessment and substantive record writing/checking stay; existing anomaly flagging earns no extra saving.

Same-system save 1 stays fully retained with no saving. Final completed entry check s4 gates exact actual content/meter/account; edits require recheck. No repair order, customer notification or bill adjustment is promised.
unknowns: Actual history lookup and exception-entry repetition
research_questions: Which fields are retyped after opening an actual flagged meter, and how are unconfirmed reasons marked?

already_counted.description: Actual physical verification, supported reason assessment and final exception entry/check

incremental.description: Maintain meter history/context views and exception field mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed actual verification/reason entry and meter/account destination checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 native context scenario below 2.9% modeled net; no physical verification or causal inference saving.

tasks.short: Inspect utility meter connections and damage

steps.what: Match the actual accessible meter to the assigned route/account and inspection scope
inputs: actual assigned route/account and inspection instructions
actual physical meter identity and access condition
outputs: reader-confirmed actual meter and inspection context

steps.what: Inspect meters for unauthorized connections, defects and damage such as broken seals, observing actual accessible condition within the inspection scope
inputs: reader-confirmed actual meter and inspection context
actual meter, connections, seals and observable condition
outputs: reader's actual inspection observations and uncertainty

steps.what: Enter and check actual meter inspection observations, defect/damage descriptions, uncertainty and intended route exception record in meter field records (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: reader's actual inspection observations and uncertainty
actual meter/account identity and existing route context
outputs: exact checked actual inspection entry and meter/route destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked actual meter inspection entry in the intended meter/route record
inputs: exact checked actual inspection entry and meter/route destination

tasks.design: Configure fixed meter/route context in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the meter field record system. The reader physically inspects the actual meter, records real observations and checks the complete entry before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated meter/account identifiers add inspection-record entry work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native route-context forms can reuse fixed identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Physical damage, seal condition and suspicious connections require actual inspection and careful descriptions.
tasks.human_edge: Report observable facts without converting suspicion into a confirmed finding.

ambition.what: No automatic tampering allegation, disconnection or repair.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; field-record owner validates access and actual inspection fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native meter-context forms can reduce repeated identifier entry while physical meter-condition inspection remains reader work.

assumptions: Unmeasured documented field-inspection episode. Gross 24 x .10 = 2.4; upkeep .75; net 1.65 hours per 100.
Reader produces actual observations in s2 and captures/describes/checks them in s3. No free structured defect classification, remote image analysis or new inspection feed.
Only fixed identifier/navigation entry changes; all inspection and actual descriptions stay. Existing route identifiers already filled today earn no saving.

Same-system save 1 stays fully retained with no saving. Final completed actual inspection entry/destination check s3 gates s4; edits invalidate it. No separate escalation message, repair order or meter action is automatically issued.
If the same field exception record also contains the abnormal-reading verification, deduplicate shared entry/context saving rather than add both.
unknowns: Actual inspection record-entry repetition and required escalation workflow
research_questions: Which actual inspection fields are retyped, and does a real escalation need its own checked send?

already_counted.description: Physical identity/condition inspection and actual final observation entry/check

incremental.description: Maintain and spot-check inspection meter/route context

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed actual inspection observations and meter/route destination checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 fixed-entry scenario below 1.65% modeled net; physical inspection and conclusions retained.
